questions.stem_latex:
The bank has approved Raj's loan of \$70000 for him to get a new car. The bank charges interest at $0.85\%$ per month. Raj pays \$2000 at the beginning of every month to pay off his loan.

The amount in the account immediately after the $n$th repayment can be determined using the recurrence relation

$$A_n=A_{n-1}(1.0085)-2000,$$

where $n=1,2,3,\dots$ and $A_0=70000$

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Calculate the amount of interest added in the first three months.

The mode occurs at the maximum turning point of this concaving down parabola. The two $x$ intercepts are $x=0$ and $x=5$. Vertex occurs at

$$x=\dfrac{0+5}{2}=2.5$$

$\therefore$ The mode of $f(x)$ is $x=2.5$

solutions.latex:
$$y=x^3-x^2-x+6$$

$$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=3x^2-2x-1$$

$$3x^2-2x-1=0\Rightarrow(3x+1)(x-1)=0$$

$x=-\dfrac{1}{3},\ x=1$; $y=\dfrac{167}{27},\ y=5$

$$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6x-2$$

At $x=-\dfrac{1}{3}$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6\times\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)-2=-4<0$

At $x=1$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6\times1-2=4>0$

$\therefore\left(-\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{167}{27}\right)$ is a max turning point, $(1,5)$ is a min turning point
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: finds both stationary points; 1: finds the correct $x$ values for the turning points

solutions.latex:
$$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6x-2$$

$6x-2=0\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{3}$

$$y=\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^3-\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^2-\dfrac{1}{3}+6=\dfrac{151}{27}$$

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&0&\frac{1}{3}&1\\\hline\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}&-2&0&4\end{array}$$

There is a change in concavity, therefore the point of inflection is $\left(\dfrac{1}{3},\dfrac{151}{27}\right)$

solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct solution; 1: correct curve with some key features shown

solutions.latex:
Particle at rest when $v=0$:

$$2-\dfrac{3}{t+1}=0\Rightarrow\dfrac{3}{t+1}=2\Rightarrow t+1=\dfrac{3}{2}\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{1}{2}\ \text{s}$$
$$\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sin x}\right)=\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x)^{-1}=-1\times\cos x\times(\sin x)^{-2}=-\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}\times\dfrac{1}{\sin x}=-\cot x\,\text{cosec}\,x$$

$$\dfrac{dV}{dr}=\dfrac{25\pi}{9}(18r-3r^2)$$

$$\dfrac{25\pi}{9}(18r-3r^2)=0\Rightarrow3r(6-r)=0\Rightarrow r=0\text{ cm},\ r=6\text{ cm}$$

If $r=0$ cm, the cylinder doesn't exist.

$$\dfrac{d^2V}{dr^2}=\dfrac{25\pi}{9}(18-6r)$$

At $r=6$ cm: $\dfrac{d^2V}{dr^2}=\dfrac{25\pi}{9}(18-6\times6)=-50\pi<0$

$\therefore r=6$ produces maximum volume.

Maximum volume is

$$V=\dfrac{25\pi}{9}(9\times6^2-6^3)=300\pi\ \text{cm}^3$$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution; 2: shows $r=6$ cm produces maximum volume; 1: obtains $r=6$ cm
